subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals (ZenHealth)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hall <jordan.hall@zenhealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals (ZenHealth)

Thanks again for taking the time today 

great conversation. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Lack of runbook-level visibility for prompt regressions across releases (hard to triage which prompt change caused quality drops)
- No consolidated production observability for model outputs (token-level latency/cost breakdowns, per-route quality metrics)
- Difficulty running controlled evals against golden prompt sets during rollouts; manual and slow

Current stack you described:
- App: internal chat assistant running on GKE -> backend calls our inference endpoints via an internal proxy
- Logging/metrics: Datadog (service metrics) + S3 for raw transcripts
- CI: GitHub Actions for app releases; no standardized model rollout guardrails today

Success criteria you mentioned:
1) Detect and alert on generation quality regressions within 2 hours of rollout
2) Per-route token cost and latency breakdown in the console (to identify expensive prompts)
3) Automated golden-prompt evals that run on every model candidate and surface regressions in a PR
4) Clear rollback / canary guardrails so engineering can safely push model changes

Requests from you on the call:
- Dashboard examples for per-route quality + token-cost (you asked for a sample dashboard)
- Tracing hooks to tag requests with session/user/context IDs for investigation
- Eval checklist and suggested golden prompt set structure

Proposed next steps:
1) I will send a one-page MAP + sample dashboards (attached).
2) We’ll provide an eval checklist & template (attached Excel).
3) Schedule a 45-min technical review with Rishi (inference ops) next week to talk tracing hooks + rollout guardrails.
4) Set up a 14-day evaluation running golden prompts against your staging traffic.

Would Thursday 3/18 or Friday 3/19 mornings PST work for the technical review?

Attachments: MAP-ZenHealth-v1.pdf (high-level mutual action plan), eval-checklist-zenhealth.xlsx (template).

Thanks 

\u0001
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Hall <jordan.hall@zenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@zenhealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: observability & evals (ZenHealth)

Thanks Marissa 

this is great and captures the call. A few clarifications and answers to your bullets: 

> Key pain points you shared:
> - Lack of runbook-level visibility for prompt regressions
> - No consolidated production observability for model outputs
> - Difficulty running controlled evals

All correct. Additional detail: our primary complaint is that a single prompt tweak in release X caused a 6% drop in operator satisfaction on the billing flow last month and we had no immediate signal tying the drop to that prompt change.

On success criteria: point 1 and 3 are highest priority for us. If we can automate regression detection and tie it back to releases, that alone would be a big win.

Technical constraints:
- Staging footprint is small; we can route a subset (~5%) of production traffic for evals and shadowing.
- We use Datadog APM but don’t currently propagate user/session IDs into model logs  



Availability: 3/18 AM PST works for the technical review. Please include Rishi from your infra team.

Attaching a short export of the operator satisfaction metric trend (last 90 days) for context.
